newsitem.title: USA: Elvis called Carter seeking help for a friend.
newsitem.headline: Elvis called Carter seeking help for a friend.

text.p: Weeks before he died, a drugged Elvis Presley called President Jimmy Carter at the White House and asked him to help a friend he believed was in trouble, The New Yorker magazine reported.

"When I was first elected president, I got a call from Elvis Presley," the magazine quoted Carter as saying in its Aug. 18 issue, available on Monday. "He was totally stoned and didn't know what he was saying. His sentences were almost incoherent."

Millions of Elvis fans will be marking the 20th anniversary Aug. 16 of the death of the King of Rock'n'Roll from a drug-induced heart attack at the age of 42. Events during Elvis Week include tours of his Graceland residence, non-stop listening to hits such as "Hound Dog", "Love Me Tender" and "Blue Suede Shoes" or watching TV specials, including one called "Elvis Meets Nixon".
In one of the more bizarre meetings between a president and a rock star, President Richard Nixon made Presley an honorary U.S. Drug Enforcement Agent in 1970.
Presley met Carter and wife Rosalynn at a 1973 concert in Atlanta when Carter was governor of Georgia.
Presley called the Oval Office in the summer of 1977 seeking a presidential pardon for a sheriff he knew who was in legal trouble, the New Yorker said.
"I talked to him for a long time, and I finally extracted that from him," Carter said.

The New Yorker said Carter patiently tried to ease the rock star out of his paranoid delusions and to calm his fears that he was being "shadowed" by sinister forces and that his friend was being framed.

"I asked him what the sheriff's sentence was, and he said that he hadn't been tried in court yet. Well I said, 'Elvis, I can't consider a pardon until after a trial and sentencing and everything.' I don't think he understood that."
Elvis continued to make desperate calls to the White House, but Carter never spoke with him again.
